title: Global Extrema on a Triangle
topic: Finding the global minimum and maximum of f(x, y) = x² + y² − xy + x + y on the triangular region x ≤ 0, y ≤ 0, x + y ≥ −3. The extreme-value theorem guarantees both extrema exist; they live among three kinds of candidate points: interior critical points (one at (-1, -1)), points where the gradient is parallel to a boundary edge (one per edge), and corners. Compare all seven candidates and the smallest and largest values are the answers. Plenum 6 problem 3 — the highest-leverage exam workout in chapter 6.

beats.narration: A continuous function on a closed bounded region always has a global minimum and a global maximum. The trick is finding them — and there are only three places they can hide.

elements.content: Manimo bobs centre, caption 'Interior. Edges. Corners.'

beats.narration: Here's the region: the triangle with x at most zero, y at most zero, and x plus y at least minus three. Inside that triangle we want the smallest and largest values of f of x comma y equals x squared plus y squared minus x y plus x plus y.

elements.content: x and y axes in chalk-200
Filled triangle with vertices (0,0), (-3,0), (0,-3) — chalk-300 stroke + amber-400 low-opacity fill
Faint contour lines of f over the triangular region
Right panel: 'the function' eyebrow + 'f = x² + y² − xy + x + y' + 'three boundary inequalities' caption

beats.narration: First place to look — interior critical points. Set the gradient to zero. That gives x equals y equals minus one, and f equals minus one. Already a strong candidate for the minimum.

elements.content: Same axes + triangle stay
Big emerald-400 dot at (-1, -1) labelled with f = -1
Right panel: 'interior critical point' eyebrow + 'grad f = 0 → (-1, -1)' + 'f(-1, -1) = -1' verdict

beats.narration: Second place to look — the three edges. On each edge, restrict f to a single variable function and minimise. You get three more candidate points, with values of minus a quarter, minus a quarter, and minus three quarters.

elements.content: Same axes + triangle stay
Dot on edge x = 0 at (0, -0.5) labelled f = -1/4 in rose-400
Dot on edge y = 0 at (-0.5, 0) labelled f = -1/4 in rose-400
Dot on edge x + y = -3 at (-1.5, -1.5) labelled f = -3/4 in rose-400
Right panel: 'edge minimisers' eyebrow + three sub-points + 'restrict, take one-variable derivative' caption

beats.narration: Third place to look — the corners. f at the origin is zero. f at the other two corners is six and six. Big numbers — the maximum is going to live here.

elements.content: Same axes + triangle stay
Dot at (0, 0) labelled f = 0 in chalk-100
Big amber-400 dot at (-3, 0) labelled f = 6
Big amber-400 dot at (0, -3) labelled f = 6
Right panel: 'corners' eyebrow + f values list (0, 6, 6)

beats.narration: Compare the seven candidates. The smallest value is minus one at the interior critical point — that's the global minimum. The largest is six, hit at two of the corners — that's the global maximum.

elements.content: 'compare candidates' mono eyebrow
Two big result cards centred: 'GLOBAL MIN  f = -1  at (-1, -1)' in emerald-400, 'GLOBAL MAX  f = 6  at (-3, 0) and (0, -3)' in amber-400

beats.narration: Three places, three checks, one comparison. That's the whole recipe.
